entries.snippet: The German-owned chain's low prices are winning over shoppers — and pushing competitors to respond.

entries.title: Can Black voting power and Trump fatigue break Mississippi's red wall?
entries.snippet: Mississippi has the largest proportional Black population in the country. It's one reason the U.S. Senate race has seen millions in last-minute spending and high-profile campaign visits.

entries.title: Polymarket has investigated 'dozens' of election-related cases
entries.snippet: The prediction market has hired a former FBI official to make sure political insiders don't use the platform for profit from confidential election information.

entries.title: Democrats still poised to make gains, but poll shows warning signs for just how many
entries.snippet: Democrats hold significant advantages going into Election Day, according to a new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll. But lagging enthusiasm among key groups is just one indicator that gains may not come easy.

entries.title: Morning news brief
entries.snippet: A new NPR poll reveals Democrats' advantage going into Election Day, congressional Democrats are forming a task force to protect the election, Netanyahu vies for reelection as polls open in Israel.

entries.title: Data centers are a hot-button issue for Ohioans as midterms near
entries.snippet: In Ohio, many people are displeased with the state's rapid buildout of data centers. It's a hot-button issue in the midterms, as political candidates from both parties try to ease voter concerns.

entries.title: Harry Kane becomes first Englishman in 25 years to win Ballon d'Or
entries.snippet: Kane was followed in the voting by Kylian Mbappé. Spain star Alexia Putellas won her third women's Ballon d'Or. Outside, fans packed the streets and climbed light poles near the London Palladium.

entries.title: Jay-Z picks himself to headline the Super Bowl halftime show in Southern California
entries.snippet: The NFL, Apple Music and Roc Nation announced Monday night that Jay-Z will be the featured performer for the halftime festivities on Feb. 14 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

entries.title: Brewers rout the Rays 10-1 to move within a win of their first World Series title
entries.snippet: The Milwaukee Brewers are one victory from their first World Series title after routing the Tampa Bay Rays 10-1 on Monday night thanks to a trio of young players who have shined in October.

entries.title: What our final poll before Election Day says about midterms and Trump
entries.snippet: Democrats hold an 8-point lead among likely voters in the fight for control of Congress with one week until Election Day, according to the latest PBS News/NPR/Marist poll.

entries.snippet: In a closely watched election, Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defeated right-wing and Trump-aligned challenger Flávio Bolsonaro. Transport and weather disruptions in parts of Brazil led to a chaotic final stretch at the polls. Bolsonaro is refusing to concede, and

entries.snippet: Brazil is not the only country to have had dramatic election results this weekend. In Serbia, longtime leader Aleksandar Vucic lost a historic election that brought down his government. William Brangham discussed the results with Heather Conley.

entries.title: Spiritual leaders unite to help keep the peace on Election Day
entries.snippet: A minister, a rabbi and an imam walk into a polling place. No, it's not the beginning of a joke, but a coordinated effort to train clergy to help keep the peace on Election Day. Deema Zein reports.

entries.title: Trump administration charges former FBI Director James Comey for the third time
entries.snippet: The Trump administration is attempting to prosecute former FBI Director James Comey for what it calls disclosing classified information, employing the unusual maneuver of bypassing a grand jury.

entries.title: Trump administration asks Washington state to set aside ballots from 400 voters it says may be noncitizens
entries.snippet: The effort is the latest by the administration to identify noncitizen voters, even though noncitizen voting is exceptionally rare.

entries.title: Tens of thousands of Israelis living abroad are expected to fly in for pivotal vote
entries.snippet: Tens of thousands of Israelis living abroad are expected to fly in for this month's election. That's according to AID Coalition, a U.S.-based nonprofit focused on strengthening Israel's democracy.

entries.title: Voters in these Democratic strongholds could ban trans girls from girls' school sports
entries.snippet: Colorado and Washington are reliably Democratic states where elected officials have rejected moves to ban transgender women and girls from female sports competitions. Now activists have gone around lawmakers to put proposed bans on both states' ballots.

entries.title: Following post-surgery checkup, Pope Leo will proceed with Latin America trip, Vatican confirms
entries.snippet: Pope Leo XIV will proceed with his planned trip to Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru from November 6 to 17.

entries.title: 1st confirmed Ebola patient in Nigeria evacuated to Switzerland
entries.snippet: A Swiss woman being treated for Ebola in Nigeria has been medically evacuated to Switzerland with her husband.

entries.title: France pledges new university admissions to quell student anger. But only after Macron leaves office
entries.snippet: The move announced on Monday seeks to quell student anger after weeks of mass protests over education and living costs.

entries.title: After a flurry of ethics cases, sexual harassment rules for Congress are under review
entries.snippet: Lawmakers reviewing the issue of sexual harassment on Capitol Hill say they're disturbed by what they've found.

entries.title: Walter Koenig, Ensign Chekov on the original 'Star Trek' series, dies at 90
entries.snippet: In "Star Trek," Ensign Chekov was the sole Communist-bloc member of the spaceship Enterprise bridge staff. His friendly, supportive presence showed how the rival nations were capable of working together.

entries.title: Catholic bishops say White House prayer photo with Trump was used politically
entries.snippet: Two Catholic bishops have expressed regret that they agreed to a White House meeting that produced a publicly distributed photo of them praying with President Donald Trump.

entries.title: A guide to the key ballot measures voters will decide on Election Day
entries.snippet: When Americans cast their ballots in this year's midterm elections, they'll not only be picking who represents them in Congress, but also weighing in on a range of topics that could change their state laws and constitutions.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: DR Congo reports over 10,000 Ebola cases as the outbreak spreads abroad, with no approved vaccine or specific treatment for the Bundibugyo virus
entries.snippet: DR Congo has reported more than 10,000 Ebola cases and nearly 4,900 deaths. The outbreak involves a virus for which there is no approved vaccine or specific treatment, complicating efforts to contain its spread.

entries.title: Germany's Merz says erosion of global order means middle powers in Europe and Asia must be more assertive
entries.snippet: During a visit to Singapore, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Europe and Germany want to increase free trade with open competition, reliability and a rules-based order.

entries.title: Two men face UK national security charges following an incident near RAF Fairford, with police suspecting Iranian state involvement
entries.snippet: British prosecutors have charged two men over an incident near RAF Fairford in September. Police suspect Iranian involvement in the case at a base used for US strikes on Iran.

entries.title: Police in northern Germany search for suspects after car ramming overnight injures several
entries.snippet: A person intentionally drove into a group of people in a northern German town, police have said. Three people have been taken into custody in what police said was likely a gang confrontation.

entries.title: India news: Arunachal sees fresh violence over proposed dam
entries.snippet: More violence erupted in India's northeastern state of Arunachal Pradesh over proposed hydroelectric projects that locals are protesting. Also, India's top court will hear pleas against the poll body chief. More on DW.

entries.title: Israel election: Israelis vote for 1st time since October 7 terror attack
entries.snippet: Israel's longest-serving prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, faces a battle to stay in power amid fierce competition from a bloc led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot. Arab parties are projected to play kingmakers.

entries.title: Brazil elections: Merz, world leaders congratulate Lula on his win
entries.snippet: Brazilian President Lula secured a surprise win over far-right challenger Flavio Bolsonaro, whose party recognizes Lula's election victory.

entries.title: Ukraine and Russia begin Oleshky ceasefire for aid mission
entries.snippet: Around 2,000 people remain stranded in the city of Oleshky, facing severe shortages of food and medicine. The Russian-occupied town has been devastated by fighting and flooding since Moscow's invasion in 2022.

entries.title: US seeks new charges against former FBI chief James Comey
entries.snippet: The Trump administration accuses the former FBI director of leaking classified information a decade ago. Comey denies wrongdoing, while his lawyers argue the case is legally invalid and comes too late.

entries.title: England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or
entries.snippet: The England captain ends his country's 25-year wait for the prestigious award after scoring 73 goals for club and country last season, beating competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.

entries.title: Jordan says its military struck 'militant hideouts' in Syria after deadly church attack
entries.snippet: Jordanian armed forces carried out strikes on "militant hideouts" in Syria that it said were linked to a deadly church attack on the kingdom last week. Syria gave a different account.

entries.title: UN sounds the alarm over Israel's West Bank military operation
entries.snippet: The UN has sounded the alarm on Israeli action in the West Bank city of Hebron after hundreds of families were displaced over the weekend. Israel has ordered the military to demolish homes after soldiers were killed.

entries.title: A bad omen? Syria bans women from university courses
entries.snippet: The recent announcement that Syrian tertiary institutes will not allow women into some courses has triggered debate. Critics worry it may be a sign that the new Syrian government is restricting women's rights.

entries.title: AI company Anthropic files its IPO in hopes of raising $100 billion
entries.snippet: Anthropic has filed paperwork for an initial public offering that could be one of the biggest in history. The co-founders have outlined both the benefits and the risks of AI in their pitch to potential investors.

entries.title: German police probe cruise ship captain after Bremerhaven collision
entries.snippet: A three-ship collision has led to the cancellation of a cruise and expensive damages. Shipyard repairs are needed, and further cruises could be affected.

entries.title: What Germany thinks of carmaker Audi's $4 billion deal with Trump
entries.snippet: The luxury carmaker is set to open its first factory in the United States — a move Trump credits to his tariffs. DW examines the German reaction amid a massive auto industry cull at home.

entries.title: Why Ukraine may be involved in Mali's conflict
entries.snippet: Allegations that Ukrainian specialists are supporting Tuareg rebels in Mali highlight Kyiv's effort to challenge Russian influence far beyond the battlefield in Europe.

entries.title: Macron vows 'strong measures' to combat protests that rocked France
entries.snippet: French President Emmanuel Macron said his government will announce "strong measures" in response to violent protests in France in recent weeks. But he also acknowledged that students have "legitimate" grievances.

entries.title: Germany's Merz in Asia as security issues loom large
entries.snippet: Chancellor Friedrich Merz will be meeting the leaders of Singapore, Japan and South Korea as Germany seeks to adjust its foreign policy to rising uncertainty and threats to global supply chains.
